text:
Marta: Heads-up: proposed mini-epic to finish airgap connector + installer UX for Private (VPC + on-prem) next sprint. Core deliverables: airgap bundle, operator-shim v3 with staged rollback, and explicit egress-preserve installer mode. Need tradeoffs called out for customers who forbid maintenance windows.

Raj: Clarify: staged rollback = canary -> partial rollback -> full rollback? We need to define what "staged" means in SLOs and automation. Also, egress-preserve will likely require static SNAT mapping or a relay during cutover. That adds ops complexity.

Devon: My proposal for staged rollback: 1) canary on 5% tenants, 2) escalate to 25% if green, 3) hold, then final 100%. Each step has a 10min observation window. Automation triggers auto-rollback on error budget breach.

Samir: Field report: BigBank will not accept any egress IP changes. They run legacy firewall rules tied to IPs. We should provide a documented "no-egress-change" mode and a support runbook for their NetOps.

Elin: Technical constraints: "no-egress-change" requires either VIP handoff with DNAT or pre-provisioned SNAT mapping. For DNAT we need L4 routing changes that the customer must apply. Let's list network pre-reqs clearly in packaging doc.

Priya: Customer comms note: offer two paths in the public-facing doc: (A) maintenance window with 30m buffer and in-place upgrade (fast), (B) zero-downtime path using relay + staged canary (longer, more complex). Call out residual latency and cost for relay.

Marta: Good split. Also: acceptance criteria draft: - In-place minor upgrades complete <15m for 90% tenants (<=2GB state). - Canary automation with rollback <=10m when triggered. - No-evidence of egress IP change in "no-egress-change" mode during test. - Airgap bundle passes offline install smoke tests.

Raj: Testing notes: include an e2e matrix: dual-stack, NAT gateway, BGP peering, private DNS with split-horizon, and KMS rotation during upgrade. Add simulated large-KV test (10GB) as a perf regression test (will be excluded from fast path).

Devon: Estimates: shim v3 polish + automation = 12 dev-days, packaging + airgap = 4 infra-days, QA for canary + egress tests = 6 QA-days. Docs + runbooks = 2 PD-days. Total ~5 dev-weeks with 25% contingency.

Elin: Draft runbook snippet to include manual validation steps:
```
# verify operator shim is running
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=operator-shim
# check upgrade health metric (promql)
upgrades:health:rate:avg{job="redwood-upgrades"}
```

Samir: Suggest adding a small console widget: per-tenant upgrade progress and a toggle to enable relay fallback. That helps Support during cutover.

Priya: I'll prepare two short email templates: maintenance-window invite + zero-downtime proposal (with cost/latency tradeoffs). Include opt-in checkbox for egress-preserve mode.

deploy-bot: nightly-ci: airgap-bundle build succeeded (2026-03-22T04:02Z) :white_check_mark:

Marta: Action items: @Devon write the staged-rollback spec + automation playbook; @Elin enumerate egress-preserve methods and network pre-reqs; @Priya draft customer comms + SLA options; @Raj add the large-KV perf test to infra queue. Review on Thursday 10:00 PT.

Raj: One more: add observability signals: per-tenant upgrade_time_seconds, egress_ip_change_events, and upgrade_stage labels. We'll need Console story for these metrics.

Marta: Added. Thanks all — aim to have the spec + rough test harness by EOD Tuesday.
